learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn the secret rule of grammar teamwork: making sure your subject and verb match perfectly in every sentence!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Just like a lock and key must fit together, a subject and its verb must match! If a subject is singular (one person or thing), the verb must be singular. If the subject is plural (many), the verb must be plural.
Here is a fun trick: Plural nouns often end in 's' (like dogs, cats), but singular action verbs end in 's' (like plays, runs)! So we say 'The dog runs' (singular) but 'The dogs run' (plural).
The pronouns 'I' and 'You' are special VIPs in grammar. Even though they refer to one person, they usually take plural verbs without an 's', like 'I play' or 'You read'.

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Grammar Matchmaker
fun_activity.instructions: Write down three singular subjects and three plural subjects. Now, draw lines to match them with the correct action verbs to make perfect sentences!

quick_recap: ⭐ The subject and verb must agree in number.
⭐ Singular subjects take singular verbs (which often end in 's').
⭐ Plural subjects take plural verbs (which usually do not end in 's').
⭐ The pronouns 'I' and 'You' are exceptions and usually take plural verbs.
